Structure, not divine purpose.old_r: Confident: this fragment only repeats that habitat may be part of a species' character, with no animal definition.
Structure, not divine purpose.new_r: This passage makes a definitional claim about species by stating that habitat/origin is part of the species' character in Agassiz's view. That is a claim about what constitutes the species, not about its function or divine purpose.

Intrinsic-nature definition.author: Ernst Haeckel
Intrinsic-nature definition.text: The whole body of the vertebrate animal, like every other many-celled organism, is a republican state of cells, and consequently it can accomplish organic functions which the individual cell, as a solitary individual
Intrinsic-nature definition.extract: The whole body of the vertebrate animal, like every other many-celled organism, is a republican state of cells, and consequently it can accomplish organic functions which the individual cell, as a solitary individual
Intrinsic-nature definition.old_r: Confident: it is only a metaphorical comparison of the body to a republic of cells, with no real definitional content completed here.
Intrinsic-nature definition.new_r: This passage gives a general characterization of what the vertebrate animal body is: a many-celled collective or 'state of cells.' That is an ontological claim grounded in internal constitution rather than divine purpose or organ function.

Intrinsic-nature definition.author: Asa Gray
Intrinsic-nature definition.text: Crystals do not grow at all in the sense that plants and animals grow. Intrinsic-nature definition.extract: On the other hand, if a response to external impressions by special movements is evidence of feeling, vegetables share this endowment with animals ; while, if conscious feeling is meant, this can be affirmed only of the higher animals.
Intrinsic-nature definition.old_r: Confident: it contrasts growth and response in general terms but does not define animals substantively.
Intrinsic-nature definition.new_r: The passage distinguishes animals by internal capacities or responsiveness—especially conscious feeling—as what can be affirmed of higher animals. That is a definitional claim about what separates kinds of living things, based on internal f

Part/organ functional characterization.text:

Part/organ functional characterization.extract: " Darwin justly mentions the greyhound as being equal to any natural species in the perfect co-ordination of its parts, ' all adapted for extreme fleetness and for running down weak prey.' "
Part/organ functional characterization.old_r: Confident: it only discusses how long evolution would take and gives the greyhound as an example, not what an animal is or does.
Part/organ functional characterization.new_r: The greyhound is characterized by parts adapted for fleetness and pursuit of prey, which is a direct functional definition of the animal's organization. No divine planner is invoked, so this is NDT.

Part/organ functional characterization.author: William Kirby
Part/organ functional characterization.text: This line, in conjunction with the rays, serves as a scaffolding for her to walk over, and it also keeps the rays properly stretched.
Part/organ functional characterization.extract: This line, in conjunction with the rays, serves as a scaffolding for her to walk over, and it also keeps the rays properly stretched.
Part/organ functional characterization.old_r: Confident: a single functional sentence about a line acting as scaffolding and stretching rays, but too fragmentary and contextless to count as a substantive definition.
Part/organ functional characterization.new_r: The spider's line is defined by what it serves for: scaffolding and keeping the rays stretched. That is a straightforward functional characterization without divine grounding.

Functionally-defined class term.author: Ernst Haeckel
Functionally-defined class term.text: Biting flies (Mordentia) comprise the most ancient and primzval winged Flies, the gauzywinged (Neuroptera), straight-winged (Orthoptera), and beetles (Coleoptera).
Functionally-defined class term.extract: Biting flies (Mordentia) comprise the most ancient and primzval winged Flies, the gauzywinged (Neuroptera), straight-winged (Orthoptera), and beetles (Coleoptera).
Functionally-defined class term.old_r: Confident: it only lists orders grouped as biting flies without explaining what makes them so.
Functionally-defined class term.new_r: The class label 'Biting flies' defines these animals by feeding function. Since a functionally defined class counts as NDT even without further elaboration, this is non_divine_teleology.

Functionally-defined class term.author: Ernst Haeckel
Functionally-defined class term.text: The majority of them were fearful beasts of prey (the Megalosaurus from twenty to thirty, the Pelorosaurus from forty to fifty feet in length).
Functionally-defined class term.extract: The majority of them were fearful beasts of prey (the Megalosaurus from twenty to thirty, the Pelorosaurus from forty to fifty feet in length).
Functionally-defined class term.old_r: Confident: this is a brief descriptive remark about being beasts of prey, without further definitional content.
Functionally-defined class term.new_r: The animals are characterized as a functionally defined class, 'beasts of prey,' which identifies them by ecological role. That makes the passage non_divine_teleology.

Functional characterization (general).author: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
Functional characterization (general).text: It is purely these last kind of causes that constitute instinct ; and seeing that they are not the produce of any deliberation, thought, or judgment, instinctive actions always satisfy surely and unerringly the wants felt and the habits acquired. Hence instinct in animals is a compelling tendency, p
Functional characterization (general).extract: Hence instinct in animals is a compelling tendency, prompted by sensations in giving rise to needs ; and it causes the execution of actions without the intervention of any thought or act of will.
Functional characterization (general).old_r: Confident: it explains instinct as a cause of action, but not what an animal is or a part is in structural terms.
Functional characterization (general).new_r: This is an explicit definition of instinct in animals by what it does: a compelling tendency causing action. Because the purposive/dispositional characterization is not grounded in God, it is NDT.

Functional characterization (general).extract: In the spring they emerge, in infinite shoals from their hiding places, and proceed southward for the purposes of depositing their eggs in more genial seas ; more than half a million of these have been discovered in a single female.
Functional characterization (general).old_r: Confident: this is mainly geographic and descriptive narrative about mackerel behavior and food use, with no real definitional account of what fish are.

Functional account, explicitly non-divin.author: William Paley
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.text: The shells of snails are a wonderful, a mechanical, and, if one might so speak concerning the works of nature, an original contrivance. Other animals have their proper retreats, their hybernacula also or winter quarters, but the snail carries these about with him.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.extract: Other animals have their proper retreats, their hybernacula also or winter quarters, but the snail carries these about with him.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.old_r: Confident: it describes the snail shell as a contrivance but gives no substantive definition of what the animal is beyond a comparison.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.new_r: The snail is characterized functionally through its shell as a portable retreat or winter quarter. This is a purposive account of the animal's covering without divine grounding.

Functional account, explicitly non-divin.author: William Paley
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.text: In some joints, very particularly in the knees, there are loose cartilages or gristles between the bones, and within the joint, so that the ends of the bones, instead of working upon one another, work upon the intermediate cartilages. Cheselden has observed*, That the contrivance of a loose ring is
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.extract: In some joints, very particularly in the knees, there are loose cartilages or gristles between the bones, and within the joint, so that the ends of the bones, instead of working upon one another, work upon the intermediate cartilages.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.old_r: Confident: it only describes loose cartilages in joints and compares them to machine hinges, without defining the animal itself.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.new_r: The loose cartilages in the knees are characterized by the role they play between the bones during motion. This is a functional description of an animal part without divine grounding.

Functional account, explicitly non-divin.author: William Paley
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.text: The use of these cartilages is to keep the passage for the air constantly open ; which they do mechanically.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.extract: The use of these cartilages is to keep the passage for the air constantly open; which they do mechanically.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.old_r: Confident: it explains the cartilages mechanically as keeping the air passage open.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.new_r: This directly states the function of the cartilages in the animal body. It is a paradigmatic non-divine teleological claim about an organ part.

Functional account, explicitly non-divin.author: William Paley
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.text: MUSCLES, with their tendons, are the instruments by which animal motion is performed. It will be our business to point out instances in which, and properties with respect to which, the disposition of these muscles is as strictly mechanical, as that of the wires and strings of a puppet.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.extract: MUSCLES, with their tendons, are the instruments by which animal motion is performed.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.old_r: Confident: it defines muscles and tendons as the instruments of animal motion, a functional/mechanical account of the parts.
Functional account, explicitly non-divin.new_r: This directly characterizes muscles and tendons by their role in producing animal motion. That is a functional definition of the parts, so it is non-divine teleology.

Part/organ defined by function.extract: The beak and caudal crests of a Tetrapturus, but the dorsal is very high and serves them for a sail when swimming; their long and slender ventrals are composed of two rays.
Part/organ defined by function.old_r: Confident: it describes the animal by its dorsal fin, ventrals, and beak/caudal crests, i.e. structural features.
Part/organ defined by function.new_r: The passage characterizes the dorsal fin by the function it serves—'for a sail when swimming'—which is a purposive account of an animal part. Because the function is not grounded in God or divine plan, it is non_divine_teleology.

Part/organ defined by function.author: Ernst Haeckel
Part/organ defined by function.text: The eighth and last order of Flies, and at the same time the only one with mouth-parts adapted to sipping liquids, consists of moths and butterflies (Lepidoptera). This order appears, in several morphological respects, to be the most perfect class of Flies, and accordingly was the last to develop.
Part/organ defined by function.extract: The eighth and last order of Flies, and at the same time the only one with mouth-parts adapted to sipping liquids, consists of moths and butterflies (Lepidoptera).
Part/organ defined by function.old_r: Confident: it identifies Lepidoptera by mouth-parts adapted to sipping liquids and their morphological perfection.
Part/organ defined by function.new_r: Lepidoptera are characterized by mouth-parts 'adapted to sipping liquids,' a direct functional description of an animal part. No divine source is invoked, so this is NDT.

Functional class / ecological role.author: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
Functional class / ecological role.text:
Order 2. — Birds of Prey. A single digit behind; anterior digits entirely free ; beak and clawti

hooked. Nocturnal Birds of Prey. Owl. Eagle-owl.
Functional class / ecological role.extract: Order 2. — Birds of Prey. A single digit behind; anterior digits entirely free ; beak and claws hooked. Nocturnal Birds of Prey. Owl. Eagle-owl.
Functional class / ecological role.old_r: Confident: the passage identifies birds of prey by hooked beak, claw, digits, and nocturnal type.
Functional class / ecological role.new_r: The class label 'Birds of Prey' is itself a functionally defined animal kind, indicating a predatory role. By the project rules, such functionally defined classes count as non_divine_teleology.
